name: alert
purpose: Prominent message block for page- or section-level status (info, success, warning, error) with a tone icon, a visually hidden localized tone prefix, optional title, actions, and dismiss button. Static by default; opt-in live role (status or alert) for messages inserted or changed after load.
whenToUse: Page- or section-level status that must stay visible until the user reads or dismisses it (for example a failed save or a service notice).
Messages that offer follow-up actions such as Retry or View details.
Messages inserted or updated in response to user actions, with live set to 'polite' or 'assertive'.
whenNotToUse: Short status next to a control or value: use Inline Message.
Transient confirmation that needs no action: use Toast.
Field validation errors: use the field's own error message and the Error Summary.
Decisions that must block the page: use Dialog (role alertdialog).
responsive: Fills its container; content wraps (overflow-wrap: anywhere) and action buttons wrap onto new lines.
rtl: Logical properties: the icon and the strong tone border sit at the inline start and the dismiss button at the inline end, in both directions.
theme: Tone pairs color-{tone}-subtle background with color-{tone}-fg icon and border; body text uses color-text (all pairs in the contrast gate). Forced-colors mode draws CanvasText borders and icons.
security: Title and string messages are rendered with textContent; Node messages are inserted as given (the consumer owns them). No HTML parsing, no inline styles except CSSOM for the visually hidden prefix. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: Unit-tested per instance; alerts are not data-driven.

limitations: Live roles only announce content inserted or changed after the live region exists; an alert rendered with the initial page is not announced (use live 'off' for static content).
After dismissal via its button, focus is not moved by the component; handle aui-dismiss to move focus to a sensible element.
Dismissal is not persisted; the consumer decides whether to render the alert again.
unsupported: Rendering HTML strings as the message (pass a Node instead).
antiPatterns: Conveying tone by color alone (the component always renders an icon and a tone prefix; do not hide them).
Stacking several alerts for the same event.
